::::{#exm-smoothing-spline-zero-penalty}

#### A barely penalized smoothing spline interpolates the data

The code below simulates 20 noisy observations of a sine curve at distinct values of $x$,
fits a smoothing spline with a tiny penalty,
and computes its training residual sum of squares:

```{r}
#| label: exm-ss-zero-penalty
set.seed(1)
sim_x <- sort(runif(20))
sim_y <- sin(2 * pi * sim_x) + rnorm(20, sd = 0.3)
sim_small_lambda <- smooth.spline(sim_x, sim_y, lambda = 1e-12)
sim_rss <- sum((sim_y - predict(sim_small_lambda, sim_x)$y)^2)
```

The training residual sum of squares is `r format(sim_rss, digits = 2, scientific = TRUE)`,
which is essentially 0 even though the data have noise standard deviation 0.3,
as @thm-smoothing-spline-zero-penalty says.
